name: Francisco Goya
findings: Uses smoky black 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 764 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, bay turns up as a small accent in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 5.9x the archive's rate (from 764 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, black coral turns up as the lightest note in 67% of the paintings that hold it, 3.8x the archive's rate (from 764 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, camel turns up as the shadow in 54% of the paintings that hold it, 9.0x the archive's rate (from 764 paintings here).
Pairs light grey with pale lilac grey more than chance would predict (3 of 764 paintings here).
Pairs light grey with silver more than chance would predict (3 of 764 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, black, dark walnut) covers 57% of his paintings here.
Keeps 3 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, black to smoky black, dark olive brown.
